title: Inverse-image compatibility of Leray comparisons on original Cech cocycle classes
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $S$ an $R$-algebra (not assumed flat), $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ separated, $U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ a finite affine open cover, $M$ a quasi-coherent module and $q\in\mathbb N$. Use the scheme, module, cohomology and base-change constructions of [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-coherent], [pqf-def-cohomology], [def-pc-base-change] and [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison], and the complexes and canonical-coordinate predicate of [lem-pc-flat-cech-base-change]. Let $c:S\otimes_R C(U,M)\to C(U_S,M_S)$ satisfy IsCechBaseChange, with no invertibility assumption. Define extendedCechCycles from the composite of scalar extension of the cycles inclusion with $c^q$, by the kernel universal property. There exist $R$-linear and $S$-linear Leray isomorphisms $e:H^q(C(U,M))\simeq HOver(f,M,q)$ and $e^\prime:H^q(C(U_S,M_S))\simeq HOver(f_S,M_S,q)$ such that for every original cycle $z$, $e^\prime([\operatorname{extendedCechCycles}(1\otimes z)])=H.baseChangeLinear(e([z]))$. This assertion concerns original cocycle classes only, before extending the cohomology map to the entire tensor product; no tensor-homology comparison is assumed.

source.place: Cohomology, functoriality of the Cech comparison; applied to the separated-case Leray comparisons in 02KH and 01XD

proof.text: Separatedness over Spec R makes every nonempty finite intersection affine. Base change preserves these affine opens and their intersections and preserves the cover; module pullback is quasi-coherent. The Cech-to-cohomology comparisons are therefore isomorphisms by affine acyclicity and Leray. Naturality for multiplication makes them linear over global functions and hence over R and S.

Apply functoriality of the augmented Cech double complexes to the adjunction unit M -> p_*p^*M. Compare injective resolutions through a resolution of the pushed-forward target resolution, as in 01FD. The tuple formula in IsCechBaseChange at b=1 identifies the cocycle map with pullback followed by restriction. The commuting augmentation diagram gives equality of its cohomology class with inverse-image Ext cohomology. This is exactly H.baseChangeLinear, before tensor extension. No preservation of homology by tensor is involved. The empty-cover, degree-zero and zero-algebra cases use the same augmentation maps.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cechBaseChange_cocycle_comparison
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsSeparated f] [Finite ι]
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤)
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (q : ℕ)
    (c : tensorCech (S := S) f U M ⟶
      cechOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f) (baseChangeCover (S := S) f U)
        (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M)) (hc : IsCechBaseChange f U M c) :
    ∃ e : (cechOver f U M).homology q ≅ ModuleCat.of R (HOver f M q),
    ∃ e' : (cechOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f) (baseChangeCover (S := S) f U)
        (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M)).homology q ≅
          ModuleCat.of S (HOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f)
            (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M) q),
      ∀ z : (cechOver f U M).cycles q,
        e'.hom ((cechOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f) (baseChangeCover (S := S) f U)
          (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M)).homologyπ q
            (extendedCechCycles f U M c q ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] z))) =
          H.baseChangeLinear (S := S) f M q (e.hom ((cechOver f U M).homologyπ q z))
